title: Performance and Reliability
description: Latency, throughput, caching, rate limiting, retries, timeouts, circuit breakers, queues, observability, and graceful degradation.

lessons.title: Latency and Throughput
lessons.summary: Latency is time per request; throughput is completed work per time period.
lessons.explanation: Latency is time per request; throughput is completed work per time period. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.
examples: A service may handle high throughput while one slow endpoint has bad latency.
interview_questions: When would you apply latency and throughput?
What failure mode appears when latency and throughput is misunderstood?

lessons.title: Caching and Rate Limiting
lessons.summary: Caches reduce repeated work; rate limits protect shared resources.
lessons.explanation: Caches reduce repeated work; rate limits protect shared resources. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.
examples: Cache reference data but invalidate it when it changes.

lessons.title: Timeouts, Retries, and Circuit Breakers
lessons.summary: Timeouts bound waiting; retries need backoff; circuit breakers stop repeated failing calls.
lessons.explanation: Timeouts bound waiting; retries need backoff; circuit breakers stop repeated failing calls. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.
examples: Unlimited retries can amplify an outage.

What failure mode appears when timeouts, retries, and circuit breakers is misunderstood?

lessons.title: Observability and Degradation
lessons.summary: Logs, metrics, and traces explain behavior; graceful degradation preserves core features during failures.
lessons.explanation: Logs, metrics, and traces explain behavior; graceful degradation preserves core features during failures. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.
examples: If recommendations fail, still return the product page.

coding_challenges.title: Performance and Reliability status classifier
coding_challenges.instructions: Implement classify_status_code(code: int) -> str. Return success for 200-299, redirect for 300-399, client_error for 400-499, server_error for 500-599, and unknown otherwise.
coding_challenges.explanation: The challenge reinforces deterministic branching, status-code categories, and local test execution.
